title: My driver was already waiting 🚖
style_prompt: dark blue cinematic night, faceless silhouette, fog, minimal interior, no text, no watermark
hook_text: At 1:15 in the morning, my ride app said my driver had arrived.

scenes.narration: At 1:15 in the morning, my ride app said my driver had arrived.
I had not ordered one. I was in my flat, in my pyjamas, about to sleep.
The app showed a map. A blue dot outside my building. Pickup, home. Destination, home.
I went to the window. A car stood at the kerb, engine running, lights off.
I opened the driver's profile. The photo was a plain grey shape. Rating, five stars. Trips, one.
The driver's name was my own. The car's plate was my plate.
I checked the street. My car was not in its space. It was the one outside, waiting.
The app buzzed. Your driver is waiting. Your driver has been waiting for four years.
I looked up. The car's door was open. The back seat light was on. Empty.
The app updated. Trip started. Passenger onboard. And down in the street, the door closed, all by itself. As if someone had just sat down. As if it was me.
So tell me. Do you get in, or walk?
